applies_why: The judge text does not use a single verse's failure to state a link or its contrary as the ground for UNDERDETERMINED; it relies on the dropped curse limb and no live link remaining.
quote: D6 vs C4 (Jeremiah 22:30): UNDERDETERMINED -- C4 pressed against the curse limb the defender dropped in [CR3] LINK 5, so no live link remains to contradict; the dropping is recorded there.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. When one verse's words carry two meanings at once, both stand; the verse is not open.
room: single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED — Reading 1: the rule reaches only a judge's stated ground of verse insufficiency; Reading 2: it reaches any underdetermination resting on lack of a live link from a single verse. I chose Reading 1.
why: The judge grounded UNDERDETERMINED on the defender's dropped curse limb and absence of a live link, not on a single verse failing to state a link or its contrary.
